question.leadin: A military operation in this country called Operation Eagle Claw was authorized only when Secretary of State Cyrus Vance took a brief vacation and was not present to oppose the plan.
question.text: Name this country that took 52 Americans hostage in 1979 and released them moments after Ronald Reagan was sworn in as President in 1981.
question.clue: This country has the 2nd largest gas reserves in the world, and is the 4th largest producer of petroleum.

swap.text: In the Battles of Issus and Gaugamela, Alexander defeated Darius III, the ruler of this large empire centered on modern-day Iran.
swap.answerHtml: the First Persian Empire [or the Achaemenid Empire, or Xšāça]
swap.clue: King Psamtik III was defeated at the battle of Pelesium near the Nile Delta by a ruler of this empire named Cambyses II.

question.leadin: Give the following related to first Persian invasion of Greece.
question.text: This "Great" Persian leader, who avenged the death of Cyrus the Great by attacking Scythia, invaded Greece after the Ionian Revolt.
question.clue: After his predecessor died of gangrene, this king and six other nobles assassinated a magician pretending to be Bardiya named Gaumata, an event described in his cliff-face Behistun Inscription.

swap.text: Leonidas' 300 Spartans were defeated by this empire's much larger force: over 2 million troops if you believe Herodotus, which scholars don't. Xerxes [zerk-zees] led this empire against the Greeks, but was defeated at the naval Battle of Salamis.
swap.clue: One ruler of this empire famously ordered the ocean to be whipped.

question.leadin: Translations of the Hebrew Bible into this language were known as targum.
question.text: Name this ancient Semitic language, used as a lingua franca in Mesopotamia and Judea. Jesus Christ spoke this language inscribed on the sarcophagus of Eshmunazar II.
question.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

swap.text: The defenders of Edessa hung a squealing pig to frighten away an elephant used by this empire's Khosrau I (KUZ-rao the first). This longest-lasting Persian dynasty rivaled the Byzantines in the Middle East.
swap.answerHtml: Sassanian Empire [or Sassanid Empire; or Sassanian Dynasty; or Sassanid Dynasty; or Eranshahr]
swap.clue: The Byzantines fought a series of wars with this empire. Shapur the Great was one ruler of this empire. It was the final, non-Islamic dynasty to rule over all of Persia.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the life of the Byzantine emperor Justinian in 532 A.D.
question.text: In September 532, Justinian signed an "Eternal Peace" with Khosrau I, a king of this empire. Another ruler of this empire captured the Roman emperor Valerian after the Battle of Edessa.
question.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

swap.text: After Roman triumvirate Crassus tried to invade this empire and failed, his was head was cut off and filled with molten gold in reference to his famous wealth.
swap.clue: It fought several wars against Tigranes the Great, who ruled (+) Armenia to the west, using its heavily armored cataphracts.

question.text: This Achaemenid public works project linked Susa, a capital in modern-day Iran, to Sardis in Anatolia. It allowed horse-mounted mail couriers to go super-fast.
question.clue: This was the name given to the ancient highway that connected Susa to Sardis in the Persian Empire. This was also the name given by the Spanish to the more notable parts of the Inca road system.

swap.text: One of Alexander's successors was this general, who founded a namesake empire which ruled the Levant, Anatolia, and Mesopotamia under kings like Antiochus Epiphanes.
swap.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the generals who carved up Alexander the Great's empire after his death, the Diadochi.
question.text: This man managed to grab the lion's share of the empire, taking Mesopotamia, Persia, and Bactria. He later fought an unsuccessful war with Chandragupta Maurya.
question.clue: This ruler, one of Alexander the Great's successors, who established a namesake Hellenistic kingdom in western Asia and was succeeded by his son Antiochus I.

swap.text: The victors at Carhae were an army of this empire founded by Arsaces I, which ruled in from the third century BCE to the third century CE before Ardashir I overthrew them and established the Sassanian empire.

question.leadin: Heleen Sancisi-Weerdenburg argued that historians relied exclusively on Greek sources on this empire and that there was no solid evidence of its actual existence.
question.text: Name these people who, according to Herodotus, built the capital of Ecbatana and were last ruled by Astyages before his Persian grandson overthrew him around 550 BC.
question.clue: Early kings of these people included Deioces and Phraortes.

swap.text: The Behistun inscription is written in Old Persian, Babylonian, and the language of these peoples, whose capital was Susa. This civilization's Old dynasties included the Awan, Simashki, and Epartid.
swap.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

question.text: Darius' rise to power is described in the Bisitun inscription, which claims that Gaumata, one of these people, pretended to be Smerdis, the brother of Cambyses II. These people, who in Sasanian times were led by a chief figure called the mowbed, are described by Herodotus as one of six Median tribes.
question.clue: Important to both the Medes and Persians were this priestly class which accomplished feats of prophecy, dream-interpretation, and sorcery later named for them.

swap.text: This Parthian Spahbed was victorious at Carrhae. He was later killed by Orodes II because his success constituted a threat to his authority
swap.clue: According to Plutarch's Parallel Lives, a commander fighting against this leader had to rescind an attempted charge when he saw that his soldier's "hands were riveted to their shields and their feet nailed through and through to the ground" by arrows.

question.leadin: Name these things about the Parthian Empire.
question.text: A man of this name fought a war against Izates and perhaps codified the Avesta as part of an Iranian Revival. The sixth and last Parthian king of this name faced trouble from the Sassanid Adrashir I.
question.clue: Septimus Severus defeated the fifth Parthian emperor with this name. The sixth emperor of this name would be defeated by the Sassanids in the early third century CE.

swap.text: One of the earliest Buddhist missionaries to China, An Shigao, was supposedly a prince of this empire, which was known as "Anxi" ("an-shee") in China. The diplomat Gan Ying visited this empire on a fact-finding mission.
swap.clue: It was ruled by the Arsacid line and supplanted by Ardashir's Sassanids.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a kingdom in Asia FTPE.
question.text: Ecbatana was the capital of this kingdom, which was absorbed into Cyrus the Great's budding Persian Empire around 550 B.C.
question.clue: The city of Nineveh was captured by his successor Cyaxares, who extended this kingdom's borders to the Halys river in Asia Minor.

swap.text: This son of Kavahd didn't care much for Mazdak or his sect and ousted them. This ruler is likely the most renowned Sassanid king and warred with Justinian after concluding the Eternal Peace with him. His grandson, the second ruler of his name, was busted up by Heraclius.
swap.answerHtml: Chosroes I (or Khosrau or Khusrav or Khosrow or Osroes or Husrev)
swap.clue: Justinian's main rival throughout his reign was this Sassanid Emperor, who prosecuted the Lazic War and defeated the Bactrians and the Hephthalite Empire during his rule from 531-579 AD.
